gap: No result ChatGPT got states, for listings under $150, how many screens a "dual" or "triple" title actually adds, so price per added screen and laptop ports per added screen cannot be compared.
standout_why: I opened three rival pages; DeskFinds under-150 returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Twelve Tabs already has part of the finding: it explains that a "dual" set and a "triple" set both add two screens and quotes a shopper needing three laptop ports, but only for $265.79 and $309.99 models. The Office Journal under-150 page lists four one-screen picks without using the terms and gives no port count or wattage. Dejaflow lists ten products and never states how many screens each adds, including the $139.00 AOKER "Dual". The normalised table for this page is not yet backed by pages I opened: the FOPO and Mobile Pixels stores returned HTTP 429 on every attempt and Best Buy product pages timed out. A rerun that reads those pages could lift this to 2.
decides: It would decide the pick only by segment, and I could not confirm it today. By Dealectric's own record in the brief (read 2026-11-18, not reopened by me), the FOPO S1 adds two 14-inch 1920×1080 screens and is under $150 through the link, which would make it the two-added-screens pick. The ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK and the listings ChatGPT showed as one-screen picks would then compete on the one-added-screen segment. Whether the UPERFECT listing ChatGPT showed at $135.99 adds one screen or two is open, and that decides whether the FOPO S1 has an under-$150 rival for two added screens.
